Michels observed that since no sufficiently large and complex organization can function purely as a direct democracy, power within an organization will always get delegated to individuals within that group, elected or otherwise.

According to Michels, all organizations eventually come to be run by a "leadership class", who often function as paid administrators, executives, spokespersons or political strategists for the organization. Far from being "servants of the masses", Michels argues this "leadership class," rather than the organization's membership, will inevitably grow to dominate the organization's power structures. By controlling who has access to information, those in power can centralize their power successfully, often with little accountability, due to the apathy, indifference and non-participation most rank-and-file members have in relation to their organization's decision-making processes. Michels argues that democratic attempts to hold leadership positions accountable are prone to fail, since with power comes the ability to reward loyalty, the ability to control information about the organization, and the ability to control what procedures the organization follows when making decisions. We all sin and come short of the Glory of God (Romans 3:23), and being a Christian does not mean you don’t sin (1 John 1:8). When we do sin, we are yielding ourselves to the devil, and giving him a free shot at us, so it is very unwise to live in sin. But if you do sin, God still loves you just the same, as Jesus has already bore our punishment for all sins, past, present and future ones. Thank God for His sending Jesus to atone for our sins. Believe on Jesus and obey Him to assure your eternal salvation (Hebrews 5:9).

Jesus came to destroy the works of the devil, and that means He came to deal with the sin issue, as the devil brought sin into this world, and is the father of all sin (John 8:44). When we sin, we are cooperating with the devil and walking in the flesh, and not in the spirit. If the Christian can die to themselves and let Christ live through them (Galatians 2:20), then they will not sin, as Christ does not sin or lead us into sin. For the Christian to live a holy life, we must die to ourselves and let the spirit lead us in all things, that we may Glorify God in all we say and do. Live for the Lord at all times. Let your light shine in this dark and corrupt world, that others may see Christ living through you. Remember that you may be the only bible that some people ever see, and how you live can influence them greatly. Praise God for Jesus!
